Maya (AE): Hey team — ACME wants to buy via AWS Marketplace but pay with their corporate card and also needs a PO + invoice for procurement. They asked for a 12-month commit discount. Can we do a Marketplace private offer that invoices to their corp card?

Liam (Sales Ops): Short answer: Marketplace purchases are billed to the buyer's AWS account/payment method. We can't route marketplace charges to an external corporate card. If they want invoices/POs, we typically do a private offer (AWS Private Offers) with invoice billing through the seller (us) or enable consolidated billing via their AWS billing account.

Maya (AE): OK, they explicitly said procurement won't accept AWS billing — must be invoiced to their AP system and they need net30. They're pushing hard. Is private offer + seller invoicing feasible?

Ranjit (Solutions Eng): Technically yes — two common patterns: 1) AWS Private Offer where Redwood invoices the customer (we handle invoicing + PO), or 2) Dedicated commitment off-market (contract with PO/MSA) and then we allocate capacity. Note: private offers still show as marketplace SKUs for license tracking, but billing path changes.

Sarah (Finance): Important constraints: our finance team needs the customer entity to be a registered billing customer in our system for net30. AWS private offers can let us invoice but we need their tax & billing details up front and an approved credit process. Also note: when we invoice for a private offer, marketplace fees/settlements timeline differ — longer reconciliation.

Nina (Legal): From T&C perspective — AWS marketplace has standard marketplace terms. If we move to a seller-invoiced private offer or off-market contract, we need an MSA + SOW or addendum. Can't alter AWS marketplace terms retroactively. If they insist on custom legal language beyond our standard MSA, that will extend timelines.

Maya (AE): Deal desk? any special approvals for a 12mo commit discount here? They want 25% off list for $X commit.

DealDeskBot: Please provide list price, target ARR, and approver chain. Discounts >20% require VP Sales + Revenue Ops approval. Private-offer commitments with invoice billing may require Finance credit checks.

Liam (Sales Ops): Can you share the rough numbers? If list is $240k ARR, 25% would be $180k ARR. We need to check discount banding and any marketplace minimums. Also AWS may require minimums for private offers. I'll check the rate-card/SKU mapping.

Ranjit (Solutions Eng): FYI the SKU mapping for their required product (real-time inference cluster) looks like:
```text
SKU: RW-RT-STD-1
List price: $0.50 / instance-hour
Est monthly list: $20,000
12mo commit (20%): $16,000/mo -> $192k/yr
Private offer SKU: RW-PO-RT-001
```
If they want 25% we can propose a private-offer price but needs deal desk ok. Also note: quantization/instance-sizing can change unit economics — recommend a short POC to validate usage before final commit.

Sarah (Finance): Action items for invoicing path: we need (1) billing entity legal name, (2) billing address & VAT, (3) PO template, (4) AP contact, (5) requested payment terms. Finance also flags that if we invoice and the customer pays via corporate card (i.e., they want us to charge their card instead of AWS), we need PCI + card processing enabled; that's slower. Prefer net30 invoice via ACH/wire.

Nina (Legal): If they insist on corporate card charging through our PSP, that introduces payment processing terms and possibly higher fees. Better to do private offer with invoice.

Maya (AE): Procurement also asked about split billing: they have two subsidiaries — one in US (AWS account) and one international that holds budget. Can we map costs across entities?

Liam (Sales Ops): Split billing across entities is messy in marketplace. For private offer invoicing we can bill the entity that holds budget. For AWS account tagging and chargebacks, they can set up consolidated billing within AWS Organizations. We'll need to coordinate with customer's cloud operations team.

DealDeskBot: Checklist for private-offer + invoice path: [SalesOps prepare PO template], [Finance run credit check], [Legal prepare MSA/SOW], [Solutions Eng provide SKU & POC plan], [Sales get VP approval for >20% discount].

Maya (AE): I'll ask ACME to confirm which legal entity will sign and whether they can accept seller invoices. For the POC — they want a 2-week eval and then decide commit. Ranjit, can you draft a minimal POC scope and estimate usage?

Ranjit (Solutions Eng): Yep — will draft a 2-week POC scope with target daily qps, expected token volumes, and dev/infra responsibilities. I'll include a low-risk runbook to cap spend.

Sarah (Finance): FYI once DealDesk approves pricing we'll need NetTerms & billing contact in Salesforce so invoicing flows. No invoices until billing onboarding is completed.

Nina (Legal): I'll prep a short MSA + invoice addendum template we can reuse for private-offer deals to speed approvals.

Maya (AE): Great — next steps: Liam to open private-offer request with AWS and check if AWS requires minimums, Ranjit to send POC scope by EOD tomorrow, Nina to prepare MSA template, Sarah to start credit onboarding checklist. I'll follow up with ACME procurement and get entity details. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Liam (Sales Ops): I'll log the action items in the deal thread and loop VP for discount approval.

Maya (AE): Thanks — will update once procurement confirms entity.
